title: Bharata thanks Guha for his hospitality
introduction: Bharata thanks Guha for having come forward to offer hospitality to him and his army. He enquires about the proper route to proceed to the hermitage of Bharadvaja. Guha assures Bharata that he along with some of his ferrymen will follow him as guides. When Guha enquires Bharata whether he has an evil intention towards Rama, Bharata clarifies him that he is proceeding to Rama?s place to bring him back to Ayodhya. When night falls Bharata along with Shatrughna and his army take rest. However Guha consoles Bharata, who has been constantly bewailing, till the nightfall.
closing: Thus completes 85th Chapter of Ayodhya Kanda of the gloriousRamayana of Valmiki, the work of a sage and the oldest epic.

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्तस्तु भरतो निषादाधिपतिं गुहम् ।
प्रत्युवाच महाप्राज्ञो वाक्यं हेत्वर्थसंहितम्
verses.iast:
evam uktaḥ tu bharataḥ niṣādādhipatim guham |
pratyuvāca mahā prāGYo vākyam hetu artha samhitam
verses.translation: Hearing those words, the highly intelligent Bharata replied toGuha, the lord of Nishadas, in words that were full of reason and meaning.

verses.devanagari:
ऊर्जितः खलु ते कामः कृतःमम गुरोह् सखे।
यो मे त्वम् ईदृशीम् सेनाम् एको अभ्यर्चितुम् इच्चसि
verses.iast:
ūrjitaḥ khalu te kāmaḥ kṛtaḥmama guroh sakhe |
yo me tvam īdṛśīm senām eko abhyarcitum iccasi
verses.translation: ?O, friend of my elder brother! Indeed, your desire to offerhospitality to my army of such a magnitude, is great.?

verses.devanagari:
इति उक्त्वा तु महा तेजा गुहम्वचनम् उत्तमम्।
अब्रवीद् भरतः श्रीमान् निषाद अधिपतिम् पुनः
verses.iast:
iti uktvā tu mahā tejā guhamvacanam uttamam |
abravīd bharataḥ śrīmān niṣāda adhipatim punaḥ
verses.translation: Having spoken these excellent words to Guha; the greatlyillustrious Bharata, possessed of great splendor, said again to Guha the kingof Nishadas (as follows):

verses.devanagari:
कतरेण गमिष्यामि भरद्वाजाश्रमम् गुह।
गहनो अयम् भृशम् देशो गङ्गा अनूपो दुरत्ययः
verses.iast:
katareṇa gamiṣyāmi bharadvājāaśramam guha |
gahano ayam bhṛśam deśo gañgā anūpo duratyayaḥ
verses.translation: ?O, Guha! By which of these two routes can I go to the hermitageof Bharadvaja? This region engulfed in waters of Ganga River is not very much easy to negotiate and is difficult to cross.?

glosses.meaning: by which of the two routes
to the hermitage of Bharadvaja? Ayam = this
isnot very much easy to cross.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा राजपुत्रस्य धीमतः।
अब्रवीत् प्रान्जलिर् वाक्यम् गुहो गहन गोचरः
verses.iast:
tasya tat vacanam śrutvā rājaputrasya dhīmataḥ |
abravīt prānjalir vākyam guho gahana gocaraḥ
verses.translation: Hearing the words of the wise prince; Guha, who roams about inwoods, with joined palms answered as follows:

verses.devanagari:
दाशाः तु अनुगमिष्यन्तिधन्विनः सुसमाहिताः।
अहम् च अनुगमिष्यामि राज पुत्र महा यशः
verses.iast:
dāśāḥ tu anugamiṣyantidhanvinaḥ susamāhitāḥ |
aham ca anugamiṣyāmi rāja putra mahā yaśaḥ
verses.translation: ?O highly illustrious prince! My ferrymen wielding their bows,and very attentive, will certainly accompany you. I too will follow you (inperson).?

verses.devanagari:
कच्चिन् न दुष्टः व्रजसि रामस्याक्लिष्ट कर्मणः।
इयम् ते महती सेना शन्काम् जनयति इव मे
verses.iast:
kaccin na duṣṭaḥ vrajasi rāmasyākliṣṭa karmaṇaḥ |
iyam te mahatī senā śankām janayati iva me
verses.translation: ?I hope you are not going to attack Rama, who is unwearied inaction. This great army of yours is begetting an apprehension in my mind.?

verses.devanagari:
तम् एवम् अभिभाषन्तमाकाशैव निर्मलः।
भरतः श्लक्ष्णया वाचा गुहम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
tam evam abhibhāṣantamākāśaiva nirmalaḥ |
bharataḥ ślakṣṇayā vācā guham vacanam abravīt
verses.translation: Bharata, whose heart resembled a taintless sky, spoke thefollowing words in smooth voice, to that Guha, who confessed his doubt asaforesaid.

verses.devanagari:
मा भूत् स कालो यत् कष्टम् नमाम् शन्कितुम् अर्हसि।
राघवः स हि मे भ्राता ज्येष्ठः पितृ समः मम
verses.iast:
mā bhūt sa kālo yat kaṣṭam namām śankitum arhasi |
rāghavaḥ sa hi me bhrātā jyeṣṭhaḥ pitṛ samaḥ mama
verses.translation: ?Let not such an occasion of wretchedness come! You should neverhave suspected me. That Rama my elder brother is indeed regarded as my father.?

verses.devanagari:
तम् निवर्तयितुम् यामि काकुत्स्थम्वन वासिनम्।
बुद्धिर् अन्या न ते कार्या गुह सत्यम् ब्रवीमि ते
verses.iast:
tam nivartayitum yāmi kākutsthamvana vāsinam |
buddhir anyā na te kāryā guha satyam bravīmi te
verses.translation: ?I am going to get back Rama who is now living in the forest. O,Guha! No other apprehension should be made by you. I am telling you the truth.?

verses.devanagari:
स तु सम्हृष्ट वदनः श्रुत्वाभरत भाषितम्।
पुनर् एव अब्रवीद् वाक्यम् भरतम् प्रति हर्षितः
verses.iast:
sa tu samhṛṣṭa vadanaḥ śrutvābharata bhāṣitam |
punar eva abravīd vākyam bharatam prati harṣitaḥ
verses.translation: Hearing the words of Bharata, Guha on his part, with his faceradiated with joy spoke again to Bharata as follows:

verses.devanagari:
धन्यः त्वम् न त्वया तुल्यंपश्यामि जगती तले।
अयत्नात् आगतम् राज्यम् यः त्वम् त्यक्तुम् इह इच्चसि
verses.iast:
dhanyaḥ tvam na tvayā tulyampaśyāmi jagatī tale |
ayatnāt āgatam rājyam yaḥ tvam tyaktum iha iccasi
verses.translation: ?You be blessed! I do not see your equal on this earth - you, whowish to renounce the empire you acquired now, even without effort.?

verses.devanagari:
शाश्वती खलु ते कीर्तिर्लोकान् अनुचरिष्यति।
यः त्वम् कृच्च्र गतम् रामम् प्रत्यानयितुम् इच्चसि
verses.iast:
śāśvatī khalu te kīrtirlokān anucariṣyati |
yaḥ tvam kṛccra gatam rāmam pratyānayitum iccasi
verses.translation: ?Assuredly your fame will traverse permanently in all provinces,as you are the very person who wishes to bring back Rama from his terribleplight.?

glosses.meaning: in all provinces. YaH tvam = as you the very person who

verses.devanagari:
एवम् सम्भाषमाणस्य गुहस्यभरतम् तदा।
बभौ नष्ट प्रभः सूर्यो रजनी च अभ्यवर्तत
verses.iast:
evam sambhāṣamāṇasya guhasyabharatam tadā |
babhau naṣṭa prabhaḥ sūryo rajanī ca abhyavartata
verses.translation: While Guha was talking thus to Bharata, the sun diffused lesslight and the night fell.

verses.devanagari:
सम्निवेश्य स ताम् सेनाम् गुहेनपरितोषितः।
शत्रुघ्नेन सह श्रीमान् शयनम् पुनर् आगमत्
verses.iast:
samniveśya sa tām senām guhenaparitoṣitaḥ |
śatrughnena saha śrīmān śayanam punar āgamat
verses.translation: The illustrious Bharata, lodging that army in camps, feltdelighted by Guha?s hospitality, returned to his camp and took rest along withShatrughna.

verses.devanagari:
राम चिन्तामयः शोको भरतस्यमहात्मनः।
उपस्थितः हि अनर्हस्य धर्म प्रेक्षस्य तादृशः
verses.iast:
rāma cintāmayaḥ śoko bharatasyamahātmanaḥ |
upasthitaḥ hi anarhasya dharma prekṣasya tādṛśaḥ
verses.translation: The high soled Bharata, whose only aim is to fulfill his duty andwho is undeserving of sorrow, indeed felt grief, born of anguish for Rama.

glosses.meaning: whose only aim is to fulfillhis duty
and who is undeserving of sorrow

verses.devanagari:
अन्तर् दाहेन दहनः सम्तापयतिराघवम्।
वन दाह अभिसम्तप्तम् गूढो अग्निर् इव पादपम्
verses.iast:
antar dāhena dahanaḥ samtāpayatirāghavam |
vana dāha abhisamtaptam gūḍho agnir iva pādapam
verses.translation: As a fire is hidden in a hollow tree while a forest is on fire, sodid Bharata?s fire of anguish burn with in his heart.

glosses.meaning: while a forest onfire is burnt up

verses.devanagari:
प्रस्रुतः सर्व गात्रेभ्यः स्वेदःशोक अग्नि सम्भवः।
यथा सूर्य अंशु सम्तप्तः हिमवान् प्रस्रुतः हिमम्
verses.iast:
prasrutaḥ sarva gātrebhyaḥ svedaḥśoka agni sambhavaḥ |
yathā sūrya aṃśu samtaptaḥ himavān prasrutaḥ himam
verses.translation: Perspiration born of fieriness of grief poured off from all hislimbs, as the snow heated by solar rays melts and flows from Himavat mountain.

verses.devanagari:
ध्यान निर्दर शैलेनविनिह्श्वसित धातुना।
दैन्य पादप सम्घेन शोक आयास अधिशृंगिणा
प्रमोह अनन्त सत्त्वेन सम्ताप ओषधि वेणुना।
आक्रान्तः दुह्ख शैलेन महता कैकयी सुतः
verses.iast:
dhyāna nirdara śailenavinihśvasita dhātunā |
dainya pādapa samghena śoka āyāsa adhiśṛngiṇā
pramoha ananta sattvena samtāpa oṣadhi veṇunā |
ākrāntaḥ duhkha śailena mahatā kaikayī sutaḥ
verses.translation: Bharata, the son of Kaikeyi was pressed by the weight of thatcolossal mountain of agony consisting of rocky caverns in the shape of settledcontemplations on Rama, minerals in the shape of groans and sighs, a cluster oftrees in the shape of depressive thoughts, summits in the form of sufferingsand fatigue, countless wild beasts in the shape of swoons, herbs and bamboos inthe form of his exertions.

glosses.meaning: by the weight of that colossal mountain of agony
consisting of rocky caverns in the shape of settled contemplations on Rama
minerals in the shape of groans and sighs
acluster of trees in the shape of depressive thoughts
summits in the form of sufferings and fatigue
countless wild beasts in the shape of swoons
herbsand bamboos in the form of his exertions.

verses.devanagari:
विनिश्श्वसन्वैभृशदुर्मनास्ततः।
प्रमूढसम्ज्ञः परमापदम् गतः।
शमम् न लेभे हृदयज्वरार्दितो।
नरर्षभो यूथहतो यथर्षभः
verses.iast:
viniśśvasanvaibhṛśadurmanāstataḥ |
pramūḍhasamjJṇaḥ paramāpadam gataḥ |
śamam na lebhe hṛdayajvarārdito |
nararṣabho yūthahato yatharṣabhaḥ
verses.translation: Thereafter, Bharata the excellent among men sighing much inmelancholy, his mind utterly confused in consequence, having obtained anextreme distress, afflicted as he was with burning fever in his breast and likea bull strayed from its herd, found no peace.

glosses.meaning: afflicted with burning fever in his breast

verses.devanagari:
गुहेन सार्धम् भरतःसमागतः।
महा अनुभावः सजनः समाहितः।
सुदुर्मनाः तम् भरतम् तदा पुनर्।
गुहः समाश्वासयद् अग्रजम् प्रति
verses.iast:
guhena sārdham bharataḥsamāgataḥ |
mahā anubhāvaḥ sajanaḥ samāhitaḥ |
sudurmanāḥ tam bharatam tadā punar |
guhaḥ samāśvāsayad agrajam prati
verses.translation: The noble soled Bharata, with his escort, met Guha too in acomposed mind. Then Guha slowly reassured Bharata again as regards his elderbrother.
